Report title: Domain-Invariant Representation Learning and Sleep Dynamics Modeling for Automatic Sleep Staging
Exclusion category: Ineligible label use or single-class anomaly detection
Primary exclusion reason: Sleep-stage labels and subject identities condition first-stage VAE priors and auxiliary classifiers; supervised contrastive loss on stage labels jointly updates the representation encoder (Sections 3.2.1–3.2.3, Eqs. 1–2). Its unlabeled contrastive term does not constitute an independent label-free representation-training stage. In addition, experiments test ordinary sleep staging on SleepEDF-20/78 and an SHHS subgroup selected for regular sleep rather than a disorder-specific clinical EEG outcome (Section 4.1).

Report title: AFSleepNet: Attention-Based Multi-View Feature Fusion Framework for Pediatric Sleep Staging
Exclusion category: Ineligible label use or single-class anomaly detection
Primary exclusion reason: The stated pre-training consists of independently training sleep-stage classification branches on the labeled training set, removing their classification layers, and freezing their feature extractors before supervised fusion/classification training. No unlabeled EEG pretext objective or conventional autoencoder reconstruction training is reported. Although pediatric OSA is represented in clinical PSG cohorts, the learning method is not eligible.

Report title: CEBRA Method: Decoding Brain Activity for Advanced Brain-Computer Interface Technology
Exclusion category: Ineligible label use or single-class anomaly detection
Primary exclusion reason: The paper explicitly selects the supervised variant of CEBRA and assigns movement-task class labels to training data for representation learning. This is a label-informed embedding method rather than a label-free EEG self-supervised pretext or conventional unlabeled autoencoder. The study includes stroke patients, but the chosen learning method fails eligibility.

Report title: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Deep Learning Approaches for EEG-based Dyslexia Detection
Exclusion category: Ineligible clinical task or EEG data
Primary exclusion reason: Despite the dyslexia-detection framing and the AE-LSTM reconstruction-based feature extractor, the actual experimental dataset is Kaggle "confused-eeg": EEG from college students watching quantum mechanics and introductory mathematics videos. The full text does not establish dyslexic versus non-dyslexic participants or a dyslexia-related clinical ground-truth outcome; therefore its empirical EEG analysis does not support the claimed disorder-specific application.

Report title: Deep Transfer Learning for Sleep Stages Classification by EEG Data
Exclusion category: Ineligible clinical task or EEG data
Primary exclusion reason: TimeNet is trained/retrained without labels using UCR time series and Sleep-EDF EEG, and its embeddings are used in wake (W0) vs stage N2 sleep-stage classification on Sleep-EDF. The paper discusses sleep disorders in background, but no diagnosed patient subgroup or neurological/psychiatric/neurodevelopmental disorder-related EEG outcome is evaluated. See Section II and Experiment Description and Results (PDF pp. 1–2).

Report title: Generating Synthetic EEG Data for Psychiatric Disorders with Variational Autoencoders
Exclusion category: Methods outside the review scope
Primary exclusion reason: The paper evaluates VAE reconstruction, synthetic psychiatric EEG feature generation and latent-space quality. Unconditional label-free VAE-1 is only a generative baseline, with no downstream disorder analysis using its learned representation. Disease-specific VAE-2/3/4 use encoded psychiatric diagnosis labels as conditional inputs to their generative models, rather than an independent label-free EEG representation-learning stage followed by disorder-related evaluation. No disorder detection/clinical downstream performance is reported. See Sections III.A–B, IV, Fig. 1, Tables I–II and Conclusions (PDF pp. 2–8).

Report title: MtCLSS: Multi-Task Contrastive Learning for Semi-Supervised Pediatric Sleep Staging
Exclusion category: Ineligible label use or single-class anomaly detection
Primary exclusion reason: MtCLSS jointly optimizes unlabeled EEG transformation recognition and contrastive losses with supervised sleep-stage classification and supervised contrastive learning on the same shared encoder. Ground-truth sleep-stage labels participate directly in representation optimization, with no independent label-free pretraining stage. The presence of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea/attention-deficit cases does not resolve the ineligible label use. Evidence: PDF pp. 1–5: Sec. I contributions; Sec. III.A–C (Eqs. 1–5), Figs. 1–3; Sec. IV.A–B (local pediatric and SleepEDF-20 cohorts).

Report title: Multi-Signal Reconstruction Using Masked Autoencoder From EEG During Polysomnography
Exclusion category: Ineligible clinical task or EEG data
Primary exclusion reason: The method is genuinely self-supervised masked multi-signal reconstruction from EEG, but the experiments use 20 healthy Sleep-EDF-20 subjects and report only reconstruction MSE across wake/REM/NREM stages. No sleep-disorder patients, disease-related downstream evaluation, or diagnostic outcomes are examined; clinical applications are only proposed. Evidence: PDF pp. 1–3: Abstract; Sec. I; Sec. II.A–C (Sleep-EDF-20 healthy cohort, masked autoencoder); Sec. III, Fig. 2 and Table I; Sec. IV–V.

Report title: Reinforcement Learning Based Prediction and Classification of Sleep Disorder
Exclusion category: Methods outside the review scope
Primary exclusion reason: Despite abstract claims of self-supervised pretraining, the implemented methods are supervised apnea/non-apnea classification (e.g., logistic regression, k-NN, decision tree, random forest, XGBoost) with SMOTE and local explanation by RIL. No reproducible unlabeled EEG pretext objective, self-supervised pretraining protocol, or conventional autoencoder reconstruction is presented. The method therefore falls outside the review scope. Evidence: PDF pp. 4–8, Sec. III.A–G; Sec. IV–V; Table I.

Report title: Toward Foundational Model for Sleep Analysis Using a Multimodal Hybrid-Self-Supervised Learning Framework
Exclusion category: Ineligible clinical task or EEG data
Primary exclusion reason: SynthSleepNet uses genuine unlabeled masked-prediction and NT-Xent contrastive pretraining, followed by linear probing and fine-tuning. Its only downstream evaluations concern generic sleep-stage classification and apnea/hypopnea event detection on SHHS, without an evaluated neurological, psychiatric, or neurodevelopmental disorder as required by Table 1. Sleep-related breathing disorders are classified separately under ICD-11 Chapter 07 (Sleep-wake disorders). Excluded for ineligible clinical scope, not for lack of SSL. Evidence: PDF pp. 1, 3–7, Sec. III–IV, Fig. 1, Tables I–II.

Report title: Multimodal explainable AI predicts upcoming speech behavior in adults who stutter
Exclusion category: Ineligible label use or single-class anomaly detection
Primary exclusion reason: The EEG representation pretext classifier was trained to predict four experimentally assigned paradigm-condition labels (WG, WAG, CW, CAW), derived from the study protocol rather than from the unlabeled EEG signal. Under the review's strict data-derived, label-free EEG pretext criterion, the use of externally supplied experimental-condition targets makes the learning paradigm ineligible for the core SSL group. Facial action-unit augmentation and cross-modal alignment do not independently establish a qualifying label-free EEG representation learning pipeline. The trial-level test split also includes participants from training, and exclusion of exact downstream test trials from pretraining is not documented; this is a risk/uncertainty, not a demonstrated train-test data leak. Disease scope (developmental stuttering) is eligible. Evidence: full text, Section 2.3.1; Section 2.3.2.1 and Table 1 (WG/WAG/CW/CAW); Sections 2.3.2.2–2.3.3 and 3.1/3.3.
